source: User-supplied 60-Hr Illinois Real Estate Broker Prelicensing (2025)
note: Transformed practice questions. Correct answers are grounded in the supplied course; distractors are newly authored.

items.topic: Ch 01 — Introduction to Illinois License Law
items.question: What is the common purpose of state real estate license laws described in the course?
choices: To guarantee every real estate transaction closes
To protect the public’s health, safety, and welfare through competent and ethical licensees
To set uniform commission rates for all brokerages
To eliminate local regulation of real estate
items.explanation: The course explains that real estate license laws protect the public’s health, safety, and welfare by promoting competence, ethics, and professionalism among licensees.

items.topic: Ch 01 — Introduction to Illinois License Law
items.question: Which Illinois Compiled Statutes chapters does the course identify as especially important to a real estate licensee?
choices: Chapters 105 and 205
Chapters 225 and 765
Chapters 454 and 765
Chapters 5 and 20
items.explanation: The course identifies Chapter 225 (Professions and Occupations) and Chapter 765 (Property) as especially important.

items.topic: Ch 01 — Introduction to Illinois License Law
items.question: In the citation 225 ILCS 454/5-20, what does 454 identify?
choices: The county where the property is located
The Real Estate License Act of 2000 and its amendments
The license renewal year
The broker’s license number
items.explanation: The course explains that 454 identifies the act containing the Real Estate License Act of 2000 and later amendments.

items.topic: Ch 01 — Introduction to Illinois License Law
items.question: Which combination matches the course’s initial managing broker licensing requirements?
choices: At least 18 years old and licensed as a broker for one year
At least 20 years old and licensed as a broker for at least two consecutive years of the preceding three
At least 21 years old and five years of sales experience
At least 25 years old and currently a sponsoring broker
items.explanation: The course states that an initial managing broker applicant must be at least 20 and have been licensed as a broker for at least two consecutive years of the preceding three years.
items.source: 60-Hr Illinois Broker Prelicensing (2025), Chapter 1 / Illinois licensing material

items.question: Which form of co-ownership can be held in unequal shares and has no right of survivorship?
choices: Joint tenancy
Tenancy in common
Tenancy by the entirety
Severalty
items.explanation: The course states that tenancy in common may be owned in unequal portions and does not include a right of survivorship.

items.question: What is a defining feature of joint tenancy?
choices: Unequal ownership shares are required
Each co-owner has an equal undivided interest and a right of survivorship
Only the unity of possession is required
A deceased owner’s share always passes through a will
items.explanation: Joint tenancy is described as equal undivided ownership with the right of survivorship and the four unities of possession, interest, time, and title.

items.question: How does a metes-and-bounds legal description operate?
choices: It lists only the tax parcel number
It starts at a point of beginning, follows directions and distances, and returns to the point of beginning
It identifies only a subdivision lot and block
It is based only on street address
items.explanation: The course defines metes and bounds as beginning at an identifiable POB, describing boundaries by courses and distances, and returning to the POB.

items.question: What legal right allows a joint tenant or tenant in common to end the co-ownership?
choices: Escheat
Partition
Subrogation
Novation
items.explanation: The course states that parties to joint tenancy or tenancy in common have the right of partition to end the co-ownership.

items.question: What does the course’s PETE mnemonic represent?
choices: Police power, eminent domain, taxation, and escheat
Possession, easements, title, and estates
Planning, environment, taxation, and encumbrances
Property, equity, tenancy, and enforcement
items.explanation: P-E-T-E is used for the government interests of police power, eminent domain, taxation, and escheat.

items.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes eminent domain from condemnation?
choices: Condemnation is the government’s right; eminent domain is the court case
Eminent domain is the right to take private property for public use; condemnation is the legal proceeding used to exercise that right
They are unrelated concepts
Eminent domain applies only to taxes
items.explanation: The course distinguishes eminent domain as the governmental right and condemnation as the legal proceeding used to exercise that right.

items.question: According to the course, how long is the Illinois statutory period referenced for an adverse-possession claim?
choices: 5 years
10 years
15 years
20 years
items.explanation: The course states that the time required to claim adverse possession in Illinois is 20 years.

items.question: If a deed restriction and a zoning ordinance impose different limits on the same property, which controls under the course rule?
choices: The newer restriction always controls
The zoning rule always controls
The more restrictive use prevails
The deed restriction is automatically void
items.explanation: The course states that when a deed restriction and zoning ordinance differ, the more restrictive use prevails.

items.question: For which homes does the federal lead-based paint disclosure rule discussed in the course apply?
choices: Homes built before 1978
Homes built before 1990
Only multifamily homes
All homes regardless of age
items.explanation: The course states that Title X requires disclosure of known lead-based paint hazards for homes built before 1978.

items.question: After receiving the property report required by the Interstate Land Sales Full Disclosure Act, what minimum rescission period does the course describe for a prospective buyer?
choices: Three days
Five days
Seven days
Thirty days
items.explanation: The course states that prospective buyers have a minimum of seven days to rescind after receiving the property report.

items.question: When a settlement service provider refers a consumer to an affiliated provider, which action is consistent with the course discussion of an affiliated business arrangement?
choices: Require the consumer to use the affiliate
Hide the ownership relationship
Disclose the affiliated arrangement and do not require use of the affiliate
Collect a referral payment unrelated to ownership
items.explanation: The course states that the affiliated business arrangement must be disclosed, the consumer may not be required to use the affiliate, and compensation is limited as described by the ownership interest.

items.question: Which situation best matches the limited federal 'Mrs. Murphy' exemption described in the course glossary?
choices: A broker-owned 20-unit building
An owner-occupied dwelling with four or fewer units, with no real estate licensee involved and nondiscriminatory advertising
Any single-family rental advertised by a broker
Any owner-occupied property regardless of size
items.explanation: The course describes a limited exemption for an owner-occupied dwelling with four or fewer units, subject to restrictions including no broker involvement and nondiscriminatory advertising.

items.question: Which common-law duty requires an agent to put the principal’s interests above the agent’s own interests?
choices: Accounting
Loyalty
Disclosure
Reasonable care
items.explanation: The course describes loyalty as putting the principal’s interests above all others, including the agent’s.

items.question: How does the course characterize transactional or facilitational brokerage in Illinois?
choices: It is the default agency relationship
It is recognized only for commercial transactions
It is not recognized as an agency relationship in Illinois
It is required when both parties are unrepresented
items.explanation: The course explicitly states that transactional brokerage is not recognized in Illinois.

items.question: When the principal withdraws from an agency relationship, what term does the course use?
choices: Renunciation
Revocation
Reconciliation
Rescission
items.explanation: The course uses revocation for withdrawal by the principal; renunciation is rejection of the relationship by the agent.

items.question: What happens to the duty of confidentiality when an agency relationship terminates?
choices: It automatically ends
It survives termination
It applies only for 30 days
It becomes the sponsoring broker’s duty only
items.explanation: The course states that confidentiality survives termination of the agency relationship.

items.question: An Illinois designated agent receives contemporaneous offers from two buyer clients on the same property. What does the course require?
choices: Keep the situation secret from both clients
Give written disclosure to all affected clients
Automatically cancel one client’s offer
Convert both clients to customers
items.explanation: The course requires written disclosure to all clients when a designated agent has contemporaneous offers from two or more clients on the same property.

items.question: When an Illinois licensee has a direct or indirect interest in property involved in a transaction, when must licensee status and interest be disclosed?
choices: Only after closing
In writing before initiating the transaction
Only if the other party asks
At the next license renewal
items.explanation: The course states that the licensee must disclose in writing their license status and direct or indirect interest before initiating the transaction.

items.question: After a brokerage agreement terminates, which duties does the course identify as continuing unless a written agreement provides otherwise?
choices: Marketing and showing property
Accounting for transaction money/property and protecting confidential information
Negotiating new offers and setting list price
Preparing appraisals and legal documents
items.explanation: The course identifies continued duties to account for transaction monies/property and to keep confidential information confidential.

items.question: Which action does the Illinois course say does NOT by itself breach a licensee’s duty to a buyer client?
choices: Showing the same property to another prospective buyer
Disclosing the buyer’s confidential maximum price without permission
Ignoring the buyer’s lawful directions
Withholding a material fact actually known to the agent
items.explanation: The course states that showing a property of interest to other prospective buyers or tenants does not itself breach the duty owed to the client.

items.question: How many total education hours does the course describe for obtaining an Illinois managing broker license?
choices: 75 hours
120 hours
150 hours
165 hours
items.explanation: The course describes 165 total hours: 120 hours tied to broker pre/post-licensing plus 45 hours of managing-broker prelicensing.

items.question: What maximum Recovery Fund liability does the course state for activities by one licensee or one unlicensed employee in one transaction or set of facts?
choices: Unlimited
items.explanation: The course states a maximum liability of $300,000, or another amount adopted by rule, for the described single-licensee/transaction situation.

items.question: For how long must records relating to a transaction of a special account be maintained according to the course?
choices: 1 year
3 years
5 years
10 years
items.explanation: The course states that records relating to a transaction of a special account must be maintained for at least five years.

items.question: Within what period must a change in designated managing broker be reported to IDFPR according to the course?
choices: 5 days
10 days
15 days
30 days
items.explanation: The course states that changes in designated managing brokers must be reported to IDFPR within 15 days.

items.question: What makes a real estate advertisement a prohibited blind advertisement under the Illinois material?
choices: It uses a photograph
It omits the sponsoring broker’s business name
It lists the property price
It appears only online
items.explanation: The course states that an advertisement for property or services that does not include the sponsoring broker’s business name is a blind advertisement and is illegal.

items.question: When an ad includes the sponsoring broker’s name plus a team or individual broker name, how must the sponsoring broker’s name compare in size?
choices: It may be smaller if a logo is present
It must be at least equal in size or larger
It must be exactly twice as large
There is no size requirement
items.explanation: The course states that the sponsoring broker’s business name must be at least equal in size or larger than the team or individual broker name.

items.question: Which auction advertisement does the course identify as deceptive or misleading?
choices: Advertising an auction date and time
Calling an auction 'absolute' or 'without reserve' when a minimum or opening bid is required
Advertising an auction online
Including the sponsoring broker’s name
items.explanation: The course identifies advertising an auction as absolute/without reserve when a minimum or opening bid is required as deceptive.

items.question: How may certain otherwise misleading words such as 'realty,' 'agency,' or 'properties' appear in an Illinois real estate team name under the course rule?
choices: Only if followed by the word 'team'
Only if written in all capitals
Only on social media
They can never be used
items.explanation: The course states that listed terms may be used in team names when followed by the word 'team.'

items.question: What does the course require for an Illinois brokerage-services contract to be enforceable?
choices: It must be oral and witnessed
It must be in writing and specify an exact termination date
It must run for at least one year
It must use a state-mandated form
items.explanation: The course states that Illinois brokerage-services contracts must be in writing to be enforceable and must include an exact termination date.

items.question: Why is specific performance particularly relevant to real estate contracts according to the course?
choices: It is limited to contracts involving services
It is generally available when the contract involves unique goods such as real property
It is the automatic remedy for every breach
It is used only to recover a commission
items.explanation: The course explains that specific performance is generally available when the contract concerns unique goods, such as real property.

items.question: Which condition is part of the course’s description of a real estate licensee qualifying as a statutory nonemployee for federal tax purposes?
choices: The licensee must be paid strictly by the hour
The licensee must work without a written contract
The licensee is properly licensed, paid for output rather than hours, and works under a written contract stating nonemployee tax treatment
The sponsoring broker must withhold all payroll taxes
items.explanation: The course lists proper licensure, output-based compensation, and a written contract stating the person will not be treated as an employee for federal tax purposes.

items.question: Which three common listing agreement types does the course identify?
choices: Exclusive right to sell, exclusive agency, and open listing
Net, option, and installment listing
Gross, net, and percentage listing
Seller, buyer, and tenant listing
items.explanation: The course identifies exclusive right to sell, exclusive agency, and open (non-exclusive) listing agreements as the three common types.

items.question: Which combination is necessary for a valid offer under the course discussion?
choices: An oral statement and estimated terms
A written offer with clear intent, definite terms, and communication to the offeree
A broker signature only
A deposit without any written terms
items.explanation: The course states that the offer must be in writing, show intent to contract, contain definite terms, and be communicated to the offeree.

items.question: What happens when a seller makes a counteroffer?
choices: The counteroffer can never be withdrawn
The counteroffer must be in writing and may be withdrawn before acceptance
The original buyer is automatically bound
The counteroffer requires court approval
items.explanation: The course states that a seller’s counteroffer must be in writing and may be withdrawn at any time before acceptance.

items.question: Under the Illinois Quinlan and Tyson rule discussed in the course, what may a real estate licensee do with an approved standardized purchase agreement?
choices: Draft new legal clauses without an attorney
Fill in the blanks with factual information; specialized language should be referred to an attorney
Rewrite the contract from scratch
Act as both attorney and broker in the same transaction
items.explanation: The course limits the licensee to filling in blanks with factual information on approved preprinted forms; specialized language requires an attorney.

items.question: What relationship does the course identify as the core contract driving the settlement process?
choices: The agreement between the lender and appraiser
The purchase contract between buyer and seller
The MLS participation agreement
The agreement between the inspector and buyer
items.explanation: The course states that the contract between buyer and seller drives the settlement process.

items.question: How does the course distinguish a comparative market analysis from an appraisal?
choices: A CMA is legally identical to an appraisal
A CMA may use some sales-comparison methodology but is not the equivalent of an appraisal
Only appraisers may compare properties
A CMA is used only for commercial property
items.explanation: The course says a CMA may use some sales-comparison methodology but is never the equivalent of an appraisal.

items.question: Which expression best describes the cost approach taught in the course?
choices: Gross income × tax rate
Cost to build − depreciation + site value
Sale price − mortgage balance
Net income + debt service
items.explanation: The cost approach develops value by estimating construction cost, subtracting depreciation, and adding site value.

items.question: Which type of depreciation does the course describe as always incurable because the cause is outside the owner’s control?
choices: Physical deterioration
Functional obsolescence
External or economic obsolescence
Accrued depreciation
items.explanation: The course states that external/economic obsolescence comes from outside the owner’s control and is always considered incurable.

items.question: For what type of property is the income approach described as most useful?
choices: Property that produces or can produce income
Vacant land only
Owner-occupied homes with no rental potential
Property with no financial records
items.explanation: The course describes the income/capitalization approach as most useful for income-producing property and property with income potential.

items.question: Which activity occurs in the primary mortgage market according to the course?
choices: Only trading existing mortgage-backed securities
Originating, underwriting, closing, and funding mortgage loans
Recording deeds at the county office
Setting local property tax rates
items.explanation: The course describes the primary market as where loans are originated, processed, underwritten, closed, and funded.

items.question: What does mortgage prequalification establish?
choices: A guaranteed final loan approval
How much a buyer may be eligible to borrow
The final appraised value of the property
A binding interest rate for the life of the loan
items.explanation: The course states that prequalification establishes how much a home buyer may be eligible to borrow.

items.question: Which situation matches the course description of illegal property flipping as mortgage fraud?
choices: A property is renovated and sold after a legitimate increase in value
Parties collude to buy low, obtain an unjustifiably inflated appraisal, and resell much higher
A buyer makes a larger down payment
A lender sells a loan on the secondary market
items.explanation: The course describes illegal flipping as involving collusion and an inflated appraisal without a valid reason for the increase in value.

items.question: What is 'loan flipping' in the course’s discussion of predatory lending?
choices: Selling a mortgage to the secondary market
Repeated refinancing with minimal or no tangible benefit to the borrower
Converting a fixed-rate mortgage to cash
Transferring title with a quitclaim deed
items.explanation: The course identifies loan flipping as repeated refinancing, usually with minimal to no net tangible benefit to the borrower.

items.question: Which set of FHA standards is stated in the course summary?
choices: 20% down and no mortgage insurance
3.5% minimum down, 31% housing-expense ratio, 43% total debt-to-income ratio, and mortgage insurance
0% down and no funding fee
10% down and a 50% total debt ratio
items.explanation: The course summary states a 3.5% minimum down payment, 31% housing expense ratio, 43% total debt-to-income ratio, and required FHA mortgage insurance.

items.question: Which statement matches the course’s description of VA-guaranteed loans?
choices: They always require mortgage insurance
They may offer no down payment and no mortgage insurance, but a funding fee applies
They require a 31% housing-expense ratio
They permit a prepayment penalty
items.explanation: The course states that eligible VA borrowers may obtain loans with no down payment and no mortgage insurance, while a variable funding fee is required.

items.question: What does the course state about USDA Rural Development Section 502 financing for eligible borrowers?
choices: It is limited to 50% financing
It may provide up to 100% financing with no mortgage insurance
It can be used only for investment property
It always requires a 20% down payment
items.explanation: The course states that eligible Section 502 borrowers may receive up to 100% financing with no mortgage insurance.

items.question: What is a real estate short sale?
choices: A sale completed in fewer than 30 days
A sale in which the lender agrees to accept less than the outstanding loan balance
A sale with no lender involvement
A foreclosure auction with a short bidding period
items.explanation: The course defines a short sale as one in which the lender agrees to accept less than the loan balance; it also warns that the process may take months.

items.question: What is marketable title as described in the course?
choices: Title that guarantees the property will appreciate
Title free from undisclosed encumbrances or defects that could expose the buyer to litigation or impair use/resale
Title that has never been recorded
Title held only by a lender
items.explanation: The course describes marketable title as free and clear from undisclosed encumbrances or defects that could expose a purchaser to litigation or interfere with use or resale.

items.question: What can a suit to quiet title accomplish?
choices: Set a property’s listing price
Resolve gaps or flaws in the chain of title and remove a cloud on title
Create a mortgage lien
Convert personal property to a fixture
items.explanation: The course explains that a quiet-title action can resolve title problems or missing links and remove a cloud on title.

items.question: What protection does a quitclaim deed provide to the grantee?
choices: Full warranty against all title defects
Warranty only for the grantor’s ownership period
No warranties; it conveys whatever interest the grantor may have
A guarantee of market value
items.explanation: The course states that a quitclaim deed conveys whatever interest the grantor may have and makes no warranties.

items.question: Is recording required for a deed to be valid according to the course?
choices: Yes, every deed is invalid until recorded
No; an unrecorded deed may be valid, though recording protects the grantee against challenges
Only quitclaim deeds must be recorded
Only deeds involving financing must be recorded
items.explanation: The course states that recording is not required for deed validity, although recording gives public notice and protects the grantee’s interest.

items.question: Which statement best matches the course description of property management licensing in Illinois?
choices: Property management never requires a real estate license
Administering, marketing, and maintaining property for a fee requires a broker or managing broker license; a residential leasing agent has a narrower residential leasing role
Only attorneys may manage property
A residential leasing agent may manage every type of commercial property
items.explanation: The course states that property-management tasks for a fee require a broker or managing broker license, while a residential leasing agent may lease and collect rent on residential property.

items.question: What document creates and governs the agency relationship between a property owner and property manager?
choices: A deed
A written property management agreement
A mortgage note
A zoning certificate
items.explanation: The course states that the owner/manager relationship is created and governed by a written property management agreement.

items.question: What is the difference between contract rent and market rent?
choices: Contract rent is what the tenant actually pays under the lease; market rent is what the property could command in the open market
Contract rent is always higher than market rent
Market rent is set by the tenant
There is no difference
items.explanation: The course defines contract rent as the rent stated in the lease and market rent as what the property could rent for in the open market if unencumbered by a lease.

items.question: Which eviction practices does the course identify as illegal in Illinois?
choices: Court-ordered eviction and emergency eviction
Self-help eviction and retaliatory eviction
Eviction after a final judgment only
Eviction for nonpayment after lawful process
items.explanation: The course states that self-help/lock-out eviction and retaliatory eviction are illegal in Illinois.

items.question: Who ultimately determines the listing price of a seller’s property?
choices: The listing broker
The appraiser
The seller
The buyer’s lender
items.explanation: The course states that the seller is ultimately responsible for determining the listing price, with the broker providing research and relevant data.

items.question: Which statement about an Illinois exclusive listing agreement is supported by the course?
choices: It may renew automatically unless the seller objects
It must have a specific ending date and cannot contain an automatic renewal clause
It must last exactly six months
It can be oral if the seller agrees
items.explanation: The course states that an exclusive listing must have a specific ending date and that automatic renewal clauses are prohibited.

items.question: If a written brokerage agreement is effective for longer than one year, what annual termination right does the course describe for the seller client?
choices: No termination right until the full term ends
The right to terminate with no more than 30 days’ written notice
The right to terminate only with 90 days’ notice
Automatic termination every six months
items.explanation: The course states that the seller client must receive an annual right to terminate by giving no more than 30 days’ written notice.

items.question: When is brokerage compensation on the sale of a property negotiated according to the course?
choices: After closing
At the time the written listing agreement is made
Only after an offer is accepted
It is fixed by the state
items.explanation: The course states that compensation is negotiated between the client and broker when the written listing agreement is made.

items.question: What is the primary purpose of a comparative market analysis (CMA)?
choices: To issue a legally binding appraisal
To estimate an approximate market value by comparing the subject with relevant nearby properties
To determine the mortgage interest rate
To replace the seller’s disclosure report
items.explanation: The course describes a CMA as comparing the subject with relevant properties that sold, are for sale, or did not sell to estimate approximate market value.

items.question: What does a seller’s net estimate represent?
choices: The property’s assessed tax value
The money the seller is expected to receive after transaction costs and expenses are paid
The buyer’s cash-to-close amount
The appraiser’s final opinion of value
items.explanation: The course describes the seller’s net as the estimated money the seller should receive after costs and expenses, including commission, are paid.

items.question: For a home built before 1978, which disclosure does the course say the seller must complete in addition to applicable Illinois disclosures?
choices: A federal lead-based paint disclosure
A flood insurance policy application
A mortgage preapproval form
A zoning variance request
items.explanation: The course states that homes built before 1978 require the federal lead-based paint disclosure information.

items.question: During transaction management for a seller, which action does the course specifically recommend regarding appraisal and contingencies?
choices: Ignore both until closing day
Verify the appraisal has been ordered and ensure contingencies are met while monitoring dates
Have the listing agent perform the appraisal
Automatically waive contingencies for the seller
items.explanation: The course advises verifying that the appraisal has been ordered, ensuring contingencies are met, and closely tracking deadlines.

items.question: Which duty is specifically listed for an Illinois buyer’s agent in the course?
choices: Withhold known material facts to protect the seller
Present offers and counteroffers in a timely manner and disclose material facts actually known to the agent
Set the buyer’s maximum offer without consultation
Guarantee financing approval
items.explanation: The course lists timely presentation of offers/counteroffers and disclosure of material facts actually known to the agent among the buyer agent’s statutory duties.

items.question: When must an Illinois licensee disclose in writing that a designated agency relationship exists and identify the designated agent?
choices: Only after an offer is written
No later than when beginning to work as a designated agent on the consumer’s behalf
At closing
Only if the buyer asks
items.explanation: The course states that the written designated-agency disclosure is due no later than when the licensee begins working as designated agent for the consumer.

items.question: After receiving designated-agency disclosure, which option does the course say a buyer may choose?
choices: Only an exclusive agreement is allowed
An exclusive agreement, a nonexclusive agreement, or continued work as an unrepresented customer
The buyer must immediately become a client
The buyer must work with multiple brokerages
items.explanation: The course describes all three choices: exclusive brokerage, nonexclusive brokerage, or continuing as an unrepresented customer.

items.question: A licensee represents multiple buyer clients interested in the same parcel. What does the course say the licensee should do?
choices: Advise the parties in writing because the situation may create a conflict of interest
Secretly choose the buyer with the highest budget
Stop showing the property to everyone
Disclose each buyer’s confidential maximum price
items.explanation: The course states that when representing multiple buyers on one parcel, the parties should be advised in writing because of the potential conflict.

items.question: What must an Illinois designated agent do when two or more buyer clients have contemporaneous offers on the same property?
choices: Disclose the situation in writing to all affected clients
Submit only the highest offer
Tell each buyer the other buyer’s confidential price ceiling
Cancel both agency relationships automatically
items.explanation: The course requires written disclosure to all affected clients, who may then decide whether to retain the agent or request another designated agent.

items.question: What risk does the course identify for a buyer who submits a backup offer?
choices: A backup offer can never become binding
If the primary contract fails, the backup buyer may become obligated to perform unless the offer was retracted before moving into first position
The seller must reject every other offer
The buyer automatically loses earnest money immediately
items.explanation: The course warns that a backup buyer may become obligated if the primary contract falls through unless the backup offer is withdrawn before it moves into first position.

items.question: A buyer wants specialized legal language added to an Illinois standardized purchase agreement. What should the licensee do?
choices: Draft the language personally
Refer the buyer to an attorney
Leave the contract unsigned but proceed orally
Ask the appraiser to draft the clause
items.explanation: The course states that licensees may fill approved blanks with factual information, but specialized contractual language requires an attorney.

items.question: Which item is a typical purchase-agreement issue the course says should be addressed?
choices: Whether the purchase is contingent on financing or sale of the buyer’s current home
The buyer’s favorite paint color
The broker’s personal tax return
The appraiser’s future employment
items.explanation: The course lists financing and sale-of-current-home contingencies among typical purchase-agreement provisions to address.

items.question: How many square feet are in one acre according to the course?
items.explanation: The course uses 43,560 square feet as one acre.

items.question: A rectangular lot measures 65 feet by 150 feet. What is its area?
choices: 8,750 square feet
9,750 square feet
10,150 square feet
12,900 square feet
items.explanation: Area = width × length: 65 × 150 = 9,750 square feet.

items.question: A rectangular lot is 65 feet by 150 feet. How many linear feet are around its perimeter?
choices: 215 feet
300 feet
365 feet
430 feet
items.explanation: Perimeter = 65 + 150 + 65 + 150 = 430 linear feet.

items.question: A lot measures 200 feet by 300 feet. Approximately how many acres is it?
choices: 0.72 acres
1.00 acre
1.378 acres
2.00 acres
items.explanation: The lot contains 60,000 square feet. Dividing by 43,560 square feet per acre gives approximately 1.378 acres.
